findings.title: Resume regression pin does not assert steps 5-6 seed green on arrival, though spec and README require it
findings.evidence:
+     the segments for steps 1 and 2 MUST carry .stepper-segment-done
+     (restored-complete glows green immediately) and step 3's MUST NOT
+     (active only).
findings.detail: Spec matrix row 7 and the README arrival read (`[done, done, active, plain, done, done, plain, plain]`) make vacuous-complete steps 5-6 green on resume arrival, but the canonical YAML pin ignores them; reverting vacuous seeding would not fail the scenario.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend the arrival assertion: segments for the vacuous-complete sections (guarantor-without-guarantor, tell_us_more) MUST also carry .stepper-segment-done on resume.
findings.verification_note: round-trip.yaml:45-51 asserts steps 1-2 done + step 3 not-done on arrival and the empty-leave pin, but no assertion covers the vacuous-complete sections (README arrival read [done,done,active,plain,done,done,...] shows steps 5-6 green). A revert of vacuous seeding would not fail the scenario.

findings.title: Spec Code Map lists only two new pure exports; three are exported and tasked
findings.evidence: +- `server/priv/static/form_stepper.js` — the fix surface: `visited` map in `initBrowser` (lines ~"Steps actually visited" block), `show()`, `updateProgress()`; new pure exports `sectionComplete` + `seedDoneStates`.
findings.detail: The Code Map sentence omits `rederiveDone`, yet the spec's own task bullet and the form_stepper.js export block both include it (`rederiveDone: rederiveDone`). Minor self-contradiction in the shipped spec.
findings.recommended_fix: Amend the Code Map line to read: new pure exports `sectionComplete`, `seedDoneStates`, and `rederiveDone`.
findings.verification_note: spec-form-resume-progress-fix.md:55 reads 'new pure exports `sectionComplete` + `seedDoneStates`' while the spec's own task bullet and the form_stepper.js export block both include `rederiveDone`. Trivial doc self-contradiction in the shipped spec.

findings.title: Evidence README miscounts the stepper=off scenario population (56 vs actual 57)
findings.evidence:
The other 56 scenarios run `stepper=off` — `initBrowser` bails before any

Verified against the tree: `find .pi/skills/form-bug-hunt/scenarios -name "*.yaml" | wc -l` returns 59, and `grep -rln "stepper: true"` matches exactly 2 files (save-resume/round-trip.yaml, stepper/stepper-happy-path.yaml), leaving 57 stepper=off scenarios, not 56.
findings.detail: Off-by-one in the shipped evidence artifact. The substantive claim is verified true (the stepper=off bail in initBrowser precedes `var done = seedDoneStates(...)`, so those scenarios never execute changed code); only the count is wrong.
findings.recommended_fix: Change "The other 56 scenarios" to "The other 57 scenarios" (59 total minus the 2 stepper:true drives).
findings.verification_note: Verified: 59 scenario YAMLs, exactly 2 with stepper: true (round-trip, stepper-happy-path) -> 57 stepper=off, not the README's 56. Substantive claim holds: initBrowser's stepperOffInSearch bail precedes `var done = seedDoneStates(...)`, so those scenarios never execute the changed code. Only the count is wrong.

findings.title: New stepper `sectionComplete` collides by name with apply_analytics.js's `sectionComplete`, which has opposite vacuous-section semantics
findings.detail: Two exported same-named predicates with deliberately divergent verdicts now live in the two files the project convention says are kept-in-sync mirrors. No runtime conflict is possible (separately loaded plain scripts, analytics is contractually untouchable), but a future sync pass copying one predicate into the other would silently break a contract.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a one-line cross-reference in each function's comment noting the other file's same-named predicate differs deliberately (vacuous-true+consent-guard vs vacuous-false) and must NOT be synced.
findings.verification_note: Verified: apply_analytics.js:254 sectionComplete returns anyRequired (vacuous-FALSE, no consent guard); form_stepper.js:307 is vacuous-TRUE + consent guard. Both files are IIFE-wrapped so no runtime collision is possible, but the files are declared mirrors (KEEP IN SYNC, form_stepper.js:43-46) — a future sync pass copying one predicate into the other would silently flip a contract. Cross-reference comments would fix.

findings.title: show() same-index guard boundary untested: form-errors initial paint could seed a green if the guard is removed
findings.detail: The i!==leaving guard is what stops the initial-paint show() from rederiving the landing step. On form-errors landing on a gating-complete-but-server-invalid step, removing it seeds a green at first paint, breaking the frozen-intent 'form-errors seeds nothing' rule. Only manual browser replay covers this; no automated test reaches the wiring.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a form-bug-hunt stepper:true scenario that submits with a filled-but-invalid field, asserts the error-page start step lacks .stepper-segment-done on arrival, or export a testable show/initial-paint seam for node.
findings.verification_note: Verified: show() is an initBrowser closure (not exported); the only automated pins are the pure functions. Initial paint calls show(model.current(), {initial:true}) so i===leaving and no rederive fires — the `i !== leaving` guard is the only thing stopping a form-errors first-paint green on a gating-complete-but-server-invalid step. No YAML scenario outside round-trip asserts segments (grep confirms); form-errors no-seed-on-arrival is manual-replay-only (README rows 07-08).

findings.title: Advisory test gate: PASS
findings.detail: P0 100%: resume seeding, empty-leave-stays-white, and the render line are unit-tested (9 new node tests, 107/107 verified passing) plus E2E-pinned in round-trip.yaml. P1 ~90%: consent guard, never-sticky rederive, form/form-errors no-seed unit-covered; one narrow form-errors wiring boundary manual-only. Overall >=80%. Mix (node unit + form-bug-hunt E2E) matches the file's documented pattern.
findings.recommended_fix: To firm the gate: automate the form-errors initial-paint segment assertion (per the boundary finding) so the manual-only README replay rows 07-08 become a durable pin.
findings.verification_note: Gate finding (advisory). Independently re-ran `node --test scripts/js-tests/*.test.js` at the reviewed sha: 107/107 pass (98 -> +9 new), matching the README baseline.

rejected_findings.evidence:
index 00000000..6ad62b96 100644
Binary files /dev/null and b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/e2e-resume-progress-2026-08-04/09-stepper-happy-path-confirmation.png differ
...
index 00000000..6ad62b96 100644
Binary files /dev/null and b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/e2e-resume-progress-2026-08-04/10-round-trip-confirmation.png differ
rejected_findings.detail: Both confirmation screenshots share blob 6ad62b96. Either the confirmation page is fully generic (one capture would do; the duplication misleads) or one scenario's evidence was copy-pasted and its confirmation was never actually captured.
rejected_findings.recommended_fix: Re-capture each scenario's own confirmation screenshot, or drop one file and state in the README that the confirmation page renders identically across both runs.
rejected_findings.verification_note: False positive. view_confirmation_page (form_pages.gleam:107-199) renders only vacancy-scoped content (property_name, address, landlord_name, attestation line) — no applicant data, no timestamps. Both suite drives ran against the same seeded vacancy (resumefix01) with the same attested path, so byte-identical confirmation PNGs (blob 6ad62b96, verified via git hash-object) are the deterministic expected render, not a missing capture. The README claims nothing the identical bytes contradict.

rejected_findings.title: Seeding indexes `sectionEls` while leave-recompute indexes `sections[].el` — index alignment never shown in the diff
rejected_findings.detail: Both paths key `done` by section index, but the diff never shows `sections` being built from `sectionEls` in the same order. Any drift (filtering, reordering) would seed or re-derive the wrong steps silently.
rejected_findings.recommended_fix: Derive both from one array (e.g. pass sections.map(function(s){return s.el;}) to seedDoneStates) or confirm in review that sections is built 1:1 from sectionEls.
rejected_findings.verification_note: False positive. form_stepper.js initBrowser builds `var sections = sectionEls.map(function (el, i) {...})` — 1:1, same order, no filtering or reordering. The lens's own alternative ('confirm in review that sections is built 1:1 from sectionEls') is satisfied by inspection; no defect exists.
